name: Zephyr
tagline: Test case management and execution tracking for QA teams, usually bolted onto Jira.

pricing.basis: per user, monthly, varies by edition (Squad, Scale, Enterprise)
pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Strip Zephyr down and it is a CRUD app: test cases in folders, test cycles, execution results, a pass/fail chart. An agent can build that against SQLite in an afternoon, and for one person tracking manual regression passes on a side project it will be genuinely fine. What you cannot rebuild is the part people actually buy: living inside Jira, linking every case to an issue and a requirement, and producing coverage and audit reports a team or an auditor accepts. The REST API that CI pipelines and test frameworks post results to is replaceable with a JUnit XML importer, but only for your own pipeline. So: yes for a solo tester, no for the reason a company writes the check.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you write test cases, group them into cycles, run through them marking pass/fail/blocked with notes, and see per-cycle results plus a JUnit XML importer for automated runs.
requirements: local disk for the SQLite file
optional: JUnit XML output from your existing test runner
whatYouLose: Bidirectional Jira sync, so cases and results no longer sit next to the issues and sprints they belong to
Requirements traceability and coverage reporting that survives an audit
The public REST API that test frameworks, CI plugins and third party tools already post results into
Team permissions, review workflows and immutable execution history across projects
Enterprise reporting: cross-project dashboards, historical trend analysis, DOORS and other ALM connectors
moatNotes: The Atlassian Marketplace distribution is half the product. Being the test management tab inside a tool the whole company already opens every morning is not a feature you can self-host.
whyPeopleStillPay: Regulated teams need to prove that a shipped requirement was tested, by whom, on which build, and that the record was not edited afterwards. That proof has to be legible to someone who does not work there. Zephyr sells the paper trail and the Jira adjacency, not the checkbox UI, and a personal SQLite app produces neither. Plus test management is inherently multiplayer: the QA lead assigning a cycle to four testers is the workflow, and single-user tooling quietly deletes it.
notes: Easy to clone for one person, pointless to clone for a team that lives in Jira.
prompt:
Build a local single-user test case management app. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non negotiable: Next.js 15 with the App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind, SQLite via better-sqlite3 with a small migration file. Server actions for mutations. One repo, `npm install && npm run dev` and it works on localhost:3000 with a `data/test.db` file created on first run.

Data model:
- Project: name, key, description.
- Folder: tree under a project, parent_id nullable.
- TestCase: project, folder, key (auto like PROJ-T12), title, objective, precondition, priority (low/med/high), status (draft/approved/deprecated), labels (comma string), ordered steps (step text, test data, expected result).
- TestCycle: project, name, description, environment, planned start/end.
- Execution: cycle, test case, status (not-executed/pass/fail/blocked/wip), executed_at, executed_by (free text), comment, per-step results.

Screens:
- Project list, then a case library with a folder tree on the left, a filterable table on the right, and bulk label/priority edit.
- Test case editor with drag-to-reorder steps and a version-agnostic "clone case" button.
- Cycle view: pick cases from the library into a cycle, then a runner screen that walks case by case, marks each step, and hotkeys P/F/B to set overall status and advance.
- Cycle report: donut of statuses, pass rate, list of failures with comments, and a CSV export.

Also build:
- A JUnit XML importer: upload a file, match testcase names to case titles or keys, create executions in a chosen cycle, list unmatched entries instead of silently dropping them.
- Full-text search across case titles and steps using SQLite FTS5.
- JSON export/import of an entire project so the data is never trapped.

Explicitly out of scope: Jira or any issue tracker integration, auth, multi-user permissions, email, audit logging, BDD/Gherkin parsing. Do not add them, do not stub them.

Keep secrets out of the code; if you add anything configurable use `.env.local` and ship `.env.example`. Write a README with the schema, the hotkeys, and a seeded demo project so the app is not empty on first launch.
